text:
The Northvale Medicines Board on 14 March 2031 announced the withdrawal of Zenthora cough syrup, pulling about 212,000 bottles from pharmacies across nine districts.

Dr. Imelda Varrenstahl, the board's Chief Safety Officer, confirmed the recall. The decision rests on Recall Notice NMB-31-0447, which identifies guaifenol as the active ingredient in the syrup and attributes the withdrawal to a labeling error in batch Z-88.

The notice, as described by the board, concerns the labeling of that batch. It does not name any other active ingredient in the product.

Pharmacies in the nine affected districts have been instructed to remove remaining stock from shelves. Consumers who hold bottles of Zenthora are advised to consult the recall notice or a pharmacist before taking further doses.

The board has not said when the withdrawn product might return to sale.
